name: JD Vance
role: Vice President of the United States (2025-present); U.S. senator from Ohio (2023-2025)
summary: Vance is a national-conservative, populist Republican who combines social conservatism, strong opposition to abortion and gender-transition care, and sharply reduced immigration with tariffs, antitrust action and sympathy for striking workers. He champions free-speech arguments against European speech rules, urges Europe to carry its own defense and favors a negotiated end to the Ukraine war, while backing Israel and treating China as the main rival.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: As vice president he said the administration believes tariffs are a necessary tool to protect American jobs and industries, citing auto manufacturing, and he backed Rubio bills with tariffs on Chinese cars as a senator.

free-trade.rationale: Argues the 'logic of globalization' failed and told Rogan the establishment line of 'pro-free trade, everything is good' lets in foreign goods that destroy native industries; supports reshoring through tariffs.

unions-good.rationale: Publicly sided with striking UAW workers in 2023, criticized right-to-work laws and courts union leaders such as Teamsters' O'Brien, though he opposed the PRO Act and the AFL-CIO scores his votes at 0%.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The earlier answer rested on Wikipedia, which points to evidence but is not evidence; his floor speeches, Voteview votes and the memoir read this pass do not state his position on it.

reviewHistory.rationale: Reported to have criticized right-to-work laws (which bar compulsory union membership or fees); the position is mentioned briefly and the Senate record on it is thin.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Introduced bills to bar undocumented immigrants and DACA recipients from federally funded health benefits and sanctuary cities from housing grants, and said Afghan refugees were being prioritized over citizens; his record concerns unauthorized immigrants more than legal ones.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Said the answer to climate concerns is to produce more American energy 'including fossil fuels'; as vice president he praised steps to cut energy costs and lift environmental regulation and called for reliable power.

limit-growth.rationale: Argues environmental rules pushed manufacturing abroad and that his administration will 'slash regulations' and 'liberate companies from stifling environmental regulations' to build and grow; he treats growth as the goal.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Asked about a climate crisis he answered 'No, I don't think there is, either'; told Rogan the carbon footprint is a distraction from 'real' environmental problems and wanted to repeal Inflation Reduction Act clean-energy credits.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on nuclear research, enrichment, keeping existing plants open or opposing public support, not on building nuclear power plants, and the statement now asks whether governments should support the construction of nuclear power plants.

reviewHistory.rationale: Told Rogan that Germany closing its nuclear plants (with coal) left it dependent on Russian gas, treating the shutdown as a mistake; he has not described a nuclear policy of his own in the sources found.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Rejects the idea that AI should automate away the labor force and says work gives dignity and purpose that welfare or leisure cannot replace.

ban-cartels.rationale: Called for breaking up Google, praised FTC chair Lina Khan's antitrust work and co-sponsored a bill ending tax-free treatment of very large mergers.

corporate-influence.rationale: Told Rogan there is a 'massive corporate lobby for cheap labor' in Congress and that health companies manipulate policy for profit; has said big tech has too much political influence.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Proposed ending the Earned Income Tax Credit marriage penalty and backed a larger child tax credit ($5,000 per child).

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Strong natalist who backed raising the child tax credit to $5,000 per child and has argued that more births and labor-force participation, not cheap imported labor, should sustain the economy and Social Security.

socialized-care.rationale: The earlier answer rested on Wikipedia, which points to evidence but is not evidence; his floor speeches, Voteview votes and the memoir read this pass do not state his position on it.

reviewHistory.rationale: Said in 2021 that 'universal day care is class war against normal people' because it subsidizes the preferences of the affluent over those of working families who raise children at home.

limit-guns.rationale: Calls himself 'a big pro-Second Amendment guy'; told Rogan gun regulation cannot solve violence and in 2022 opposed background-check, red-flag and semi-automatic-weapon laws.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: At Munich he condemned EU officials who warned they might shut down social media during civil unrest; this is a criticism of one proposal, not a general statement.

party-controls-media.rationale: Munich and Paris speeches condemn government pressure to censor media and online speech and warn AI must not become a tool of authoritarian censorship.

democracy-best.rationale: Told European leaders that democracy rests on 'the sacred principle that the voice of the people matters' and that they should embrace what voters say 'even when you don't agree'.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Argued at Munich that governments need democratic mandates, cannot win them by censoring opponents, and that dismissing citizens' views destroys democracy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes a 'leadership class' that has failed ordinary workers, officials who ignore voters, and political figures motivated by defense-industry money (told Rogan).

voter-id.rationale: Told Rogan that without voter ID 'you're inviting fraud' and dismissed the argument that it is racist.

suppress-opposition.rationale: At Munich he said 'you cannot win a democratic mandate by censoring your opponents or putting them in jail' and rejected firewalls against populist parties.

traditional-family.rationale: Repeatedly argues for the traditional nuclear family, marriage and children as central to society and has urged policy to favor family formation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted against the Respect for Marriage Act and said marriage is between a man and a woman as a Catholic, while accepting same-sex marriage as the law of the land and saying the issue is not 'alive'.

abortion-legal.rationale: Opposes abortion and supported overturning Roe v. Wade; in 2024 he said states should set abortion law and denied supporting a national ban, and he backs access to mifepristone. Earlier (2022) he said he would like abortion illegal nationally.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Said pursuing 'racial or gender equity' as a value system leads to misery and sponsored a bill to end federal diversity programs.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Speaks of 'biological males' and 'biological females' as distinct categories when arguing against transgender athletes in girls' sports.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: In April 2023 he said on the Senate floor that he worries the country is 'going too far, too fast' on transgender ideology, prescribing treatments, surgeries and hormonal therapies, and criticised a diplomat for pushing its 'most leftwing versions'.

reviewHistory.rationale: Introduced the Passport Sanity Act to block an 'X' passport marker, objected to gender-identity census questions and proposed a federal ban on gender-affirming care for minors.

experts-over-public.rationale: Argues that citizens are not 'interchangeable cogs' and that voters' views should drive policy; attacked the 'public health establishment' and incumbent-driven regulation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Called mass migration the most urgent challenge facing Western nations, opposes amnesty and in October 2025 said much lower legal immigration would be better for the United States.

open-borders.rationale: Supports a border wall, ended-crossings enforcement and opposes amnesty; calls border security a core priority.

nation-first.rationale: Frames policy as 'America first', says America's interests are sometimes distinct from allies' and Catholic 'ordo amoris' means loving one's own nationals first, while still saying the US wants partners.

force-without-un.rationale: Defended US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites in 2025 and the Venezuela operation; the sources do not record him discussing UN approval itself.

national-mission.rationale: Said he made the mistake of supporting the Iraq War, that he had been lied to by the foreign-policy establishment, and warns against regime-change efforts in Iran.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said in 2024 the US does not want to leave NATO and wants Europe to take on more of its own defense while the US shifts focus.

close-ties-china.rationale: Calls China the biggest threat to the United States, backs tariffs against it, and told the Paris summit that partnering with authoritarian tech suppliers chains nations to an 'authoritarian master'.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: On 19 October 2023 he voted for the Senate resolution standing with Israel against terrorism (97-0).

reviewHistory.rationale: Strong supporter of Israel, which he calls a real ally sharing common values, and backed standalone Israel aid; has not framed this as a statement about a right to statehood.

reviewHistory.rationale: In March 2025 he said the US 'can't just ignore the president's desires' to acquire Greenland and warned Denmark and rival powers; contested because it is a stated aim of the president he repeated.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Argues that love of country and protecting American workers go together, framing the economy as America first and pro-worker.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A cited summary says he supports raising the minimum wage, but in a March 2025 speech he declined to comment on its wisdom.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Cast the tie-breaking vote for the 2025 law that made the 2017 individual rates permanent and said the administration cut taxes bigly; he has backed taxes on university endowments and mergers but not on the wealthy generally.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mixed: as a student in the memoir he took the side of payday lenders against a bill to restrict them, and in 2025 he promised the biggest deregulation in history, but he also backs antitrust action and Big Tech limits.

cut-welfare.rationale: As Vice President he cast the tie-breaking vote on 1 July 2025 for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which added work requirements and cuts to Medicaid and food assistance.

reviewHistory.rationale: Mixed: the memoir describes neighbours gaming food stamps and a minority content to live on the dole, yet says his own aid (Pell grants, loans, old-age benefits) helped and that poor kids should eat; in 2025 he voted for cuts and in 2026 framed them as fraud control.

empower-police-military.rationale: Voted against the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act on the ground that it would weaken the military amid the China threat; nothing located on police funding.

more-religion-public.rationale: The memoir presents church attendance as promoting good habits and calls for churches that engage the world (ch. 6, conclusion); he defended Ten Commandments displays in schools in 2026 and criticised limits on religious expression in Munich.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said at the 2024 convention that America is not just an idea but a nation with a shared history, whose newcomers are admitted on its terms to preserve continuity; the memoir expresses deep patriotism (ch. 11).

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Criticised a one-world governance structure for AI in 2026; no statement found on the UN.

political-violence-never.rationale: Told the 2024 convention after the attempt on Trump that there has been enough political violence.

separate-church-state.rationale: Argued that displaying the Ten Commandments in classrooms does not force religion on non-Christians, while saying faith must never be forced and a balance must be struck.

military-superiority.rationale: Opposed the 2023 debt-limit deal for weakening the military against China, and told the 2024 convention that when America punches it punches hard.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Defined the nation by shared history and a common future, said citizens come first whatever the colour of their skin and spoke warmly of his wife's immigrant family.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Wants more electricity and data centers to win the AI race with China, but also told AI builders to stop if they are building a Frankenstein.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Backs American Compass proposals for workers' councils and wants normal workers to hold real authority over their working lives, though he has not proposed votes on running large companies.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Mixed: he calls the deficit a serious problem and criticises both parties on spending, but he voted for the 2025 law that raised the debt ceiling by $5 trillion and cut taxes.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Treats Christian faith as a guide to life, reading Leo XIII and citing John Paul II; the memoir calls for a church community that gives kids purpose.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Broke the Senate tie for the 2025 law adding Medicaid and SNAP work requirements for able-bodied adults; the memoir's chapter 9 also describes working people's resentment of those who stay on benefits.

class-collaboration.rationale: Praised cooperative union models in which workers and employers negotiate as partners rather than in zero-sum conflict, and said past cooperation between studios and community groups worked.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Said newcomers are welcome but on the nation's terms, to preserve continuity of the national project; he did not say they must give up their culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: The earlier answer rested on Wikipedia, which points to evidence but is not evidence; his floor speeches, Voteview votes and the memoir read this pass do not state his position on it.

reviewHistory.rationale: In 2022 he said Democrats wanted to bring in new voters to replace those already here, which critics called Great Replacement rhetoric; he denied racist intent, and the claim is about political advantage.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

trade-surplus.rationale: Described the globalist economy as one that borrows to buy what other countries make and presented reshoring as the remedy; he never stated a goal of exporting more than importing.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Criticised EU institutions in Munich and said voters backed Brexit to regain control of migration.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Called birthright citizenship an absurdity of the 14th Amendment and the June 2026 Supreme Court ruling upholding it a major mistake.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Defended the 2025 foreign aid cuts, objecting to sending taxpayer money to NGOs abroad.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Argued for a negotiated settlement that would have Ukraine cede some territory, which treats Russian-held land as bargainable.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Criticised European courts for annulling an election and in February 2025 wrote that judges cannot control the executive's legitimate power; he has not said courts should never constrain majorities.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Rejected the idea that other countries can or should be turned into the United States, though he praises democratic principle universally in Munich.

religion-illusion.rationale: Describes himself as returning to the Christian faith and presents religion as a source of purpose and good habits (memoir chs. 6, 15; 2026 interview), not as an illusion.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Cited Leo XIII's encyclical in 2026 as describing a middle way between child labor in factories and socialism, and said unchecked wealth concentration leads to communism or fascism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Said the solution to AI's risks is giving normal people actual authority over their own lives, through unions and competition.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Said that if wealth created by AI goes to a few the result is communism, compared it with the robber barons who led to fascism and communism, and said trusts can outweigh a vote.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Argued in 2026 that workers need a real say at the bargaining table and favoured more flexible union bargaining like some European systems, drawing on American Compass proposals; no bill of his sets wages by bargaining.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: As Vice President he cast the tie-breaking vote on 1 July 2025 to pass the One Big Beautiful Bill Act with its work requirements and cuts to Medicaid and food assistance programs.

reviewHistory.rationale: Mixed: the memoir describes neighbours gaming food stamps and a minority content to live on the dole, yet says his own aid (Pell grants, loans, old-age benefits) helped and that poor kids should eat; in 2025 he voted for cuts and in 2026 framed them as fraud control.
